value.body: A two-year postgraduate pharmacy degree after B.Pharm, regulated by the Pharmacy Council of India. Students specialise in an area such as pharmaceutics, pharmacology, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmaceutical analysis, quality assurance, regulatory affairs or pharmacy practice, and complete a research project.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 semesters; the second year is mostly a research project

items.label: Scholarship for GPAT-qualified
items.value: ₹12,400 a month for up to 24 months
items.note: For eligible students in approved programmes

value.title: How you get in
value.body: B.Pharm from a PCI-approved college. Admission is through GPAT (conducted by NBEMS) or university / state entrance tests; NIPERs run their own joint entrance for their master's programmes.

value.title: At a glance
items: A valid GPAT score at the time of admission is generally needed for the scholarship.
Specialisation shapes the career: analysis and QA lead to quality roles; pharmacology to research and drug safety; pharmaceutics to formulation.
M.Pharm is the usual minimum for teaching in pharmacy colleges, and a PhD helps for promotion.
